content.title: Composition

Why boundaries help
content.text: A small function with a clear input and output is easier to reason about than one giant block of instructions. Scope keeps temporary names close to the work that uses them.

content.question: What is one benefit of local scope and small functions?

options.text: They make all programs shorter automatically.
They limit where names are used and make individual jobs easier to reason about.
They remove the need for variables.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. They limit where names are used and make individual jobs easier to reason about.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. They limit where names are used and make individual jobs easier to reason about.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Good programs are built from small named pieces whose inputs, outputs, and names have clear boundaries.
**Senior habit:** When a function becomes difficult to explain in one sentence, look for a smaller job hiding inside it.
nextSteps: Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
